turn_complete.narrative: You asked about a doubling in denial rate. It did not double — 7.1% → 7.9% vs prior year (2025-01-01..2025-08-02), rose 0.8 points, a 11.5% relative change, short of the 100.0% a doubling assumes. The direction the question assumes is right and the size is not, so nothing below may be described in the question's own words for it. What follows is the composition of the movement that did happen. Within 2026 the denial rate by month moved from 7.3% in January to 9.1% at the last settled point, a rise of 1.9 points over six periods, with July 2026 held out as provisional (F2); that within-year climb is the context for the smaller year-over-year picture, in which the denial rate went from 7.1% to 7.9%, up 0.8 points or 11.5% in relative terms (F1). For scale, both figures sit far below the external reference of 19–20 percent of in-network claims denied reported by ACA marketplace (HealthCare.gov) issuers for 2023–2024 (F1), so the increase is real but starts and ends from a low base. One measurement note governs how these numbers should be read: claims still awaiting their first remittance (status OPEN) are excluded from both the current and prior periods, so the denial rate describes only adjudicated claims rather than the full book (F1, F2). The 9.1% figure is also the high of the settled series, not a peak set by the provisional month (F2). The last point of this series (2026-07) is RIGHT-CENSORED — it was computed over 1,544 adjudicated records against a series median of 6,050 (25.5% of it), so the month is still settling and the records that have settled are not a random sample of it. It is published as provisional and excluded from the first-to-last movement, the high and the low. A rise that terminates on an incompletely adjudicated bucket is a data-maturity artifact until that bucket matures.

metric_display.display_name: Unbilled open inventory on a running filing clock
metric_display.caveat: Counts every unbilled open claim regardless of runway, so claims a year from their deadline and claims already past it are both in the total; cut by filing_runway_bucket to separate them.
metric_display.rationale: The formula filters on billed_flag = false AND status = OPEN and applies no deadline predicate. Until 2026-08-09 none could be expressed at all, and the id — served at $22.4M in a warehouse whose genuine timely-filing anomaly cards total roughly $62K — read as a claim about exposure. The claim -> plan -> filing rule join now exists (filing_runway_bucket), and it reports that 47% of that $22.4M is already EXPIRED and 33% has more than 90 days of runway. The total is still a population rather than an exposure, so the entry stays; it is no longer a proxy for something unmeasurable, so the label does not.

metric_display.caveat: Counts discharged accounts that have not been billed; it says nothing about whether the delay is a coding backlog, a documentation hold, or a payer-side gate.
metric_display.rationale: "DNFB" is unambiguous inside revenue cycle and opaque outside it, and this metric leads the portfolio's largest card. The expansion is the whole entry; the caveat only bounds what the number diagnoses, and no formula change is implied.

items.title: DNFB accumulation: Northgate general-surgery discharges
items.description: Federal Medicare / Northgate Regional Hospital / General Surgery: 22 unbilled discharges totaling $178,217 in window 2026-07-03..2026-07-29.
items.impact_reconciliation_note: The detection system reported $178,216.82 for this cell over 2026-07-03..2026-07-29. This platform re-derived $195,873.92 from the governed dnfb_dollars contract. The two are not comparable: the governed contract is a snapshot (an as-of balance at the watermark) and applies no start..end window, while the card's figure was computed over one, so the gap between them is a difference of measurement kind rather than of population, window or valuation basis. The difference is not attributed to the detector, and this card is excluded from the divergence count.
items.ranked_on_note: ranked on the detection system's figure ($178,216.82): this platform's re-derivation is not a comparable quantity (an as-of balance against a windowed flow), so substituting it would change the claim rather than correct it.
items.actionability_rationale: Discharged-not-final-billed dollars are not lost, only unbilled: the account exists, the charges exist, and finishing the bill recovers them. The small unrecoverable residue is the coding or documentation gap that never closes. Deliberately below DUPLICATE's certainty and above every recovery category — DNFB is the cheapest money in the portfolio, which is exactly why it should outrank larger, harder items.

drill_dimension_repoints.rationale: Procedures bind at claim_line, so a claim-grain contract cannot be cut by `proc_group` at all. `primary_proc_group` is the claim's dominant procedure group (largest share of billed charges, ties broken by name), certified at the claim and transaction grains. Read the drill as an attribution of whole claims, not a decomposition of lines: the detector counted lines in this group, and the drill counts claims whose largest procedure group is this one.

items.actionability_rationale: Remitted-but-unpaid cash mostly arrives without anyone doing anything; the impact figure is timing, not loss. The workable slice is the residue where the remit never converts — unpostables, offsets and takebacks — so this scores low on purpose. A payment-lag anomaly belongs on the worklist for what it predicts about the payer, not for dollars to go chase.

Their score is floored to the median of the value-ranked work so they stay visible without displacing it.
